questions.stem: Why do root cells lack chloroplasts, even though they are plant cells?

options.text: Chloroplasts are only found in animal cells
Root cells are too small to contain chloroplasts
Roots are underground and receive no light, so photosynthesis cannot occur there
Root cells have extra mitochondria instead of chloroplasts

questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are only found in the green parts of plants that receive light, such as leaves. Root cells are underground with no light, so chloroplasts would serve no purpose as photosynthesis requires light energy.
